_meta.indication: JOENJA is indicated for the treatment of activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) syndrome (APDS) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (R, DB, PC, MC) trial of leniolisib 70 mg PO BID versus placebo PO BID
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older with activated PI3K delta syndrome (APDS)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline at Day 85 in the log10 transformed SPD of index lesions on MRI/CT, and change from baseline in percentage of naïve B cells out of total B cells
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean treatment difference in change from baseline at Day 85 in log10 transformed SPD of index lesions was -0.25 (95% CI -0.38, -0.12; p=0.0006), and in naïve B cells was 37.30 (95% CI 24.06, 50.54; p=0.0002), both favoring leniolisib

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were headache (24% vs 20% placebo), sinusitis (19% vs 0%), and atopic dermatitis (14% vs 0%). Seven (33%) patients receiving JOENJA developed an ANC between 500 and 1500 cells/microL.
target_moa: Leniolisib is a small molecule selective inhibitor of the PI3K delta catalytic subunit p110δ; overactive PI3Kδ drives APDS, and leniolisib inhibits the mutant enzyme and reduces pAKT pathway activity.

advisory_committee.vote: A Pulmonary and Allergy Drug Advisory Committee (PADAC) Meeting was not convened for this application.

summary.text: Leniolisib received a traditional (full) approval under a Priority review NDA, supported by one adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trial with confirmatory evidence. It had Orphan Drug Designation for APDS (granted January 30, 2018) and rare pediatric disease designation (August 26, 2020), and the approval conferred a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. It was the first product approved for APDS.

citations.quote: The recommended regulatory action for this NDA is **approval** of leniolisib for the treatment of APDS in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. This will be the first product approved for the treatment of APDS.

Substantial evidence of effectiveness for leniolisib in subjects with APDS was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial, with confirmatory evidence.
